trigger: Suspected security incident affecting city building systems, the owner's accounts in them, or city data the owner holds
notify: City IT manager (and the city facilities manager for anything affecting doors or equipment)

obligation: Report to the prime for GSA IT
citation: GSA BTTRG v3.0 section 1.6.1 (through the prime contract) and the CT-F subcontract
trigger: Any incident that may involve GSA building systems, GSA data (including the CUI drawings and FCI), the owner's PIV card, or GSA credentials
deadline: Immediately on discovery (the prime reports to GSA IT immediately)
notify: Prime contractor's security officer and project manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if GSA systems, data, or credentials may be involved. In an intrusion into city systems, check whether the same laptop or suite account holds CUI or FCI

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the city
trigger: Breach of security of a system the owner maintains that holds city personal information (cardholder exports)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. The 24-hour contract notice comes first
notify: The city (it gives the notices to individuals); the owner provides all information the city needs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, as treated - counsel to confirm whether the exports are personal information under 501.171(1)(g) and whether the city is a covered or governmental entity for this section

obligation: City notices to cardholders and the Department of Legal Affairs (customer duty)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: Individuals and the Department (if 500 or more Floridians) no later than 30 days after determination; consumer reporting agencies if more than 1,000 individuals. The 312 cardholders are under both thresholds
notify: Given by the city; the owner supplies facts and a timeline

obligation: City report to the state (customer duty)
trigger: The city determines a ransomware incident or a severity level 3, 4, or 5 cybersecurity incident
deadline: City reports no later than 48 hours after discovery (12 hours for ransomware); the owner's 24-hour notice must reach the city well before that
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff (by the city); the owner supplies facts, including when city data was last backed up

trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident
deadline: City submits within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service (by the city); the owner supplies input

trigger: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment identified in a system during contract performance (for example, found while investigating an intrusion at the federal building)
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days
notify: Through the prime to the GSA contracting officer

trigger: Kaspersky Lab covered article identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days
notify: Through the prime to the GSA contracting officer

trigger: Covered article or source subject to a FASCSA order provided or used in contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days
notify: Through the prime to the GSA contracting officer

citation: FAR 52.204-9(a)-(b) (flowed down); GSA PIV procedures in the CT-F subcontract
trigger: PIV card lost, stolen, or possibly copied
deadline: Immediately (CT-F subcontract notice term; POL-01 7.9), so the prime can have GSA revoke the card

citation: Fla. Stat. 282.3186; OFAC advisory (Sept. 21 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: The city may not pay or otherwise comply with a ransom demand; the owner must not pay on its behalf. Any payment for the owner's own systems needs counsel's advice and an OFAC sanctions check first

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Intrusion into building control or access control systems
deadline: As soon as practical, coordinated with the city (the city also reports to FDLE and the sheriff)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

trigger: Affected cardholders who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law (through the city)
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected cardholders; all three city buildings are in Florida

trigger: Unauthorized disclosure of federal tax information
deadline: Immediately, no later than 24 hours after discovery
notify: TIGTA and the IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: No - the owner holds no FTI

trigger: Suspected incident involving criminal justice information
deadline: Immediately, no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: The agency's incident handlers and CJIS contacts
applies_at_this_tier: No - the city police station is outside CT-C; no CJI access

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25, and the proposed government facilities criteria cover government entities, not their contractors; recheck when final
